It expanded the scope of locus standi (the legal right to file a petition), thereby making access to courts easier even for socially and economically deprived sections. However, the expression used in Assertion (A)— “necessary for the rule of law”—claims PIL to be an essential/indispensable condition, which is not correct. The rule of law in India is based on institutional and constitutional arrangements such as the basic structure of the Constitution, the principle of equality (Article 14), the right to constitutional remedies (Article 32), the writ jurisdiction of High Courts (Article 226), judicial review, etc. These existed even before the evolution of PIL, and the rule of law can continue to exist even without PIL. Thus, PIL strengthens and promotes the rule of law, but it is not an indispensable condition for its existence. Therefore, (A) is false.
